column1: # Transcribed from table_en4.pdf, Table 3 ("Positions which allow for line
# adjustment by interletter space-reduction" -- JLReq's own reduction-priority
# reading, Appendix D). Reconciled cell-for-cell against an independent Japanese
# transcription of table_ja4.pdf; every cell here is corroborated by at least one
# of: (a) both locale PDFs agreeing byte-for-byte on rect fill color and printed
# text, extracted directly with pdfplumber rather than read by eye a second time;
# (b) Table 1's already-attested amount at the same (before, after) coordinate,
# via D.1's own rule that Table 3's unadjusted amount is Table 1's; (c) a D.2 note
# or the §3.8.3 prose naming the stage explicitly.
# Two cells are recorded here as ADJUDICATED, not as a plain re-typing of either
# transcription, because the two PDFs genuinely differ at these coordinates:
#   (cl-02, cl-29): table_en4.pdf has no fill rect at this cell (matches the
#   0-em amount Table 1 records at cl-02,cl-29, and matches cl-02,cl-02's own
#   blank cell -- invariant 12's cl-01/cl-02 vs cl-28/cl-29 mirroring). table_ja4.pdf
#   has a genuine medium-gray (CMYK 0,0,0,0.45 -- stage 5) fill rect at the same
#   coordinate with no printed amount text, confirmed by a full row-cluster count
#   (24 filled cells in the JA PDF's cl-02 row against 23 in the EN PDF's, the
#   single extra cell landing exactly at cl-29). Read as "blank" in both files:
#   a stray fill artifact in the Japanese rendering, not a real datum, because
#   nothing in Table 1 or the D.2 notes gives it an unadjusted amount to reduce.
#   (cl-27, cl-25): table_en4.pdf fills this cell light gray (CMYK 0,0,0,0.1),
#   the same hue as the other 85 "1/4-1/8" cells, and §3.8.3's own numbered list
#   (id293, its sixth and last step) names exactly this reduction -- the quarter
#   em between Japanese-script text and Latin-script/numeral text, reducible to
#   an eighth em -- as the sixth priority. table_ja4.pdf fills the SAME coordinate
#   dark gray (CMYK 0,0,0,0.7, the stage-4 hue used nowhere else in a "1/4-1/8"
#   cell). Read as "1/4-1/8 stage 6" in both files: the Japanese rendering's color
#   at this one cell is treated as a document defect, on the strength of the
#   English rendering's agreement with the 85-cell pattern and with §3.8.3's prose.
# Both of the above are genuine table_en4.pdf/table_ja4.pdf divergences, not
# transcriber error on either side -- exactly the class of disagreement ADR 0009
# says this project records rather than silently resolves. There is currently no
# derived-stage only, per docs/design/generation.md's "Recorded defects" section,
# and requires a detector over spec/snapshot/, which a PDF is not). Recording the
# adjudicated reading in both files keeps `just attest` green; the reasoning above
# is the record until a spec/captured/divergences.tsv (or equivalent) exists.
# Five cells (cl-02,cl-26 / cl-05,cl-26 / cl-07,cl-26 / cl-26,cl-01 / cl-26,cl-05)
# print a colored rect with no amount text in BOTH PDFs alike -- not a divergence,
# a shared omission. Each is filled in from Table 1's already-attested amount at
# that coordinate (D.1: "the default unadjusted spacing shall be determined
# according to §B") with the floor read from the printed color, e.g. cl-02,cl-26
# is Table 1's "1/2 be" reduced at the observed medium-gray/stage-5 hue, matching
# every other "1/2-0 stage 5" cell of cl-02's row. table5.en.tsv, transcribing
# the structurally closest sibling appendix, faced the same three-coordinate
# anomaly (cl-02,cl-26 / cl-07,cl-26 / cl-26,cl-01) and chose the more
# conservative reading -- leaving the literal printed token (blank) in place and
# recording the same circumstantial case as an open question rather than as a
# value. That choice and this one are both gate-safe (Value::Blank is exempt from
# unadjusted-amount-is-table1; a filled Ranged token that matches Table 1 passes
# it). This file resolves rather than defers, per this milestone's brief, on the
# strength of the additional cross-check available here: both table_en4.pdf and
# table_ja4.pdf agree on fill color at all five coordinates (not merely one
# locale, which is all a single-table reconciliation can check), so the
# integrator reconciling all six tables may want to unify on one convention.
# Three cells cite a D.2 note instead of printing an amount (cl-05,cl-05 /
# cl-06,cl-05 / cl-07,cl-05 -- D.2 notes 1 through 3). The amount is Table 1's at
# that coordinate; the floor and stage are read from the D.2 note text quoted in
# cl-06,cl-05 (D.2#2) is a one-part reduction: only the trailing middle dot's quarter
# em moves in Table 3 (the full stop's own half em is rigid throughout, per D.2#2's
# text and every other table's reading of this coordinate), at stage 4, so the token
# states the full unadjusted amount and the floor after only that part reduces --
# cl-07,cl-05 (D.2#3) is NOT the same shape: D.2#3's Japanese text states plainly for
# Table 3 that BOTH the comma's own half em (its own priority, stated elsewhere in
# this file's cl-07 row as stage 5) and the trailing middle dot's quarter em (stage 4,
# the same priority D.2#1 and D.2#2 give cl-05 in Table 3) reduce to solid --
# "前に配置する読点類（cl-07）の二分アキ及び後ろに配置する中点類（cl-05）の四分アキを
# ベタ組まで詰める調整が可能である". A single cell of one color cannot encode two
# different stages for its two components, so the crate's evaluator does not read
# this cell at all for this one coordinate: `jlreq-spacing::evaluate::special_reduction`
# hand-splits it into its true two-stage form (stage 4 for the middle dot's own
# component, stage 5 for the comma's own component, both floors zero), which is the
# worked example ADR-0014 itself cites. This TSV's single (floor, stage) pair is kept
# only for provenance and for `xtask attest`'s cross-checks, which cannot express two
# stages either; it records the cell's *final* achievable floor (0, once stage 5's
# cumulative reduction has applied) at the *later* of the two governing stages (5),
# because a token of "stage 4" would misstate the cell as reaching 0 before the
# comma's own component is eligible to move. Earlier revisions of this file gave this
# cell "3/4-1/2 stage 4" by over-applying cl-06,cl-05's one-part shape to a cell that
# is genuinely two-part; that reading is retired here.
# cl-05,line-end (D.2#5, stage 3) is recorded as 1/4-0: Table 1's cl-05,line-end
# is "1/4 be" (B.2#4: "the preferred spacing... is a quarter em", one term). D.2#5's
# English text and §3.8.3 step 3's (id290) English text both say "before and
# after", unqualified; their Japanese halves both say specifically middle dots
# Japanese "before and after" literally would total 1/2 em, in tension with Table
# 1's single term. This transcription keeps Table 1's attested amount (1/4) so
# `unadjusted-amount-is-table1` holds; the tension is left open here rather than
# silently resolved either way, for a future reader with the raw PDF glyph layout.
# (line-head, line-end): both PDFs print "×" at this coordinate (confirmed by direct
# word extraction), matching table1.en.tsv's own line-head/line-end cell. Recorded
